To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified five acetogenins in the leaves of the Annona cheremola tree and we have developed an innovative approach to improve the bioavailability of these molecules by using supramolecular polymer micelle.

(i) the isolation of ACG isomers from A. cheromola leaves is reported for the first time, (ii) SMPMs are synthesized to encapsulate ACGs, (iii) the bioavailability of ACGs is improved by the use of SMPMs, (iv) the cytotoxicity of ACGs encapsulated in SMPMs is increased.
(i) ACGs were isolated for the first, from A. cherimoila deciduous leaves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of ACG from A. cherimoa leaves and the development of nanocarriers to enhance the bioavailability properties of annonacin.
the development of new anticancer drugs based on natural compounds and the use of nanocarriers for their administration.
the development of new strategies to improve the bioavailability and efficacy of ACGs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
A. cherimolas deciduous leaves are a rich source of ACGs and that their use as nanocarrier to improve bioavailability properties of annonacin is promising.
A. cherimolas deciduous leaves are a promising source of bioactive compounds and the use of SMPMs could be an alternative to increase the bioavailability and efficacy of ACGs.
the use of byproducts of Annona cherimoa, their pure compounds and their encapsulation into SMPMs, are a promising source of antitumor compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of by-products of A. cherí­­­­­mola and their pure compounds could be promising source for anticancer agents, while the use of supramolecular polymer micelle as a nanocarrier of annonacin could be an alternative to their application in the food field as nutra- ceutical to enhance their administration and efficacy.
the bio-guided fractionation of A. cherimoa leaves led to the isolation of five ACGs, which were encapsulated in SMPMs to enhance their bioavailability.
we have isolated for the first times some acetogenins from Anonaceae and we have improved the bioavailability of the most active acetogenin, annonacin, by encapsulating it in supramolecular polymers.

the use of by-products of A. cherí­­­­mola as a source of ACGs is promising.
